name: Times club monthly special crossword No 285

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Graduate wearing formal top returned old conductor’s cloak

indicators.note: something returned is sent back the way it came, so these letters are read from right to left
whoever is wearing clothes sits inside them, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a DJ, or dinner jacket, is formal evening wear for the upper body
Sir Charles Hallé was a nineteenth-century conductor who founded the Manchester orchestra
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder

explanation.surface: A graduate dresses up and wears a dead conductor's cloak, perhaps for a costume party.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ plus ELLAH makes DJELLAH, and the graduate sits inside it before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: A djellabah is a loose hooded robe worn in North Africa, a kind of outer garment like a cloak.

clue.text: One way to clean Caledonian Canal when temperature plummets

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining a verb

indicators.note: a letter that plummets falls straight down, so in this down entry it drops to the bottom and the order changes

blocks.note: a ditch is a channel of water, a rough canal
T stands for temperature; it names the letter that moves, which is already in the canal

explanation.surface: A Scottish canal is cleaned out when the weather turns freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of DITCH falls to the foot of the column, giving DICHT. Caledonian means Scottish, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicht is a Scots verb meaning to wipe, which is one particular method of making something clean.

clue.text: Score-settler shot exposed CIA squealer

indicators.note: to expose something is to strip its outer covering, leaving only the core
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the agency's initials with their outer letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An informer from the CIA is shot dead as revenge for some score.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the squealer a victim; both words are wordplay, and the score is a match score. Equaliser is also slang for a gun, which suits the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: An equaliser is the goal that levels a match, so it settles the score at parity between both teams.

clue.text: Ultimately driven under through being framed by chiefly deadly hulk

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
chiefly means mostly, so the word loses its last letter
a picture framed by something is surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside another
in a down entry, coming under means being placed after the rest

blocks.note: lethal is a synonym of deadly
via means by way of, or through
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Driving through a dangerous wreck, an image of some deadly hulking ship.
explanation.walkthrough: LETHA, deadly without its tail, frames VIA; the last letter of driven sits under it all.
explanation.definitionFit: A leviathan is anything enormous, especially a huge ship, which matches a hulk's sense of a massive bulky vessel or creature.

clue.text: Arguably rusty or smutty manner of speaking linked to solver outside church beginning to tear into singer

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
one thing outside another wraps around it
putting something into another places it inside

blocks.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
an idiom is a characteristic way of expressing oneself
the solver is the person addressed as you
CE is the Church of England
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crude, rusty way of talking is blamed on the solver and a church, which drives a singer to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rusty or smutty' looks like a description of crude talk, but rust and smut are fungal plant diseases. The solver's pronoun is split open to take in the church and the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust and smut fungi belong to the Basidiomycetes, the club fungi, so anything rusty or smutty in that technical sense qualifies.

clue.text: Totty bothers rich husband, cutting through source of poison

indicators.note: totty is an old word meaning dizzy or unsteady, so the letters reel into a new order
a blade that is cutting goes into its target, so one piece lies within another

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband
per means by means of, or through

explanation.surface: An attractive woman pesters a wealthy husband, a scene from a tabloid seduction plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Totty reads as British slang for attractive women, but here it is Spenser's word for dizzy. H cuts PER, and everything is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Christopher is baneberry, a woodland plant whose berries are highly toxic, so it is a botanical origin of poison.

clue.text: Cycling around commonest part of Rajasthan, keep firm hold on turban

indicators.note: cycling moves the end round to the front, as on a wheel
to go around something is to surround it

blocks.note: to grip is to keep a firm hold
this letter appears three times in the state's name, more than any other

explanation.surface: Cycling across Rajasthan, a rider grips their turban against the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIP's last letter rotates to the front to give PGRI, which then wraps round the A. Rajasthan is a state in north-west India, where turbans are common.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagri is the Indian word for a turban, the long cloth wound about the head.

clue.text: Shifting ecstasy, menials who’ll be on the right side of dealer?

definitions.text: who’ll be on the right side of dealer

indicators.note: a letter that is shifting moves to a new position, so the order changes

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy; it names the letter that moves, already among the menials
peons are labourers or drudges

explanation.surface: Drug-dealing underlings hope to stay on the right side of their dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface dealer sells drugs; the real one deals cards. Only the E moves, from second to fourth place.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the pone is the player seated to the dealer's right, who cuts the pack.

clue.text: Composer disheartened over hooded jacket

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the centre, so the middle letter goes

blocks.note: Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian composer
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A depressed composer pulls on a hooded jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Grieg loses his central I; an over in cricket is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A grego is a short thick hooded coat worn in the Levant, a type of hooded outer garment.

clue.text: Informed about what gutted family accompanying someone admits

indicators.note: a gutted thing has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters
to admit is to let in, so one group of letters holds another
about suggests turning around and moving, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: kin are one's relatives
with means together with, accompanying
one can mean a person, someone

explanation.surface: A heartbroken relative confides in someone who is privy to the secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Gutted reads as British slang for upset, but here it strips the middle out of the family word; the rest is then mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the know is an idiom for having inside knowledge, being well informed about something.

clue.text: Perhaps Orcadian pens cursive works

indicators.note: to work something is to knead and reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from Orkney writes elegant joined-up handwriting with their pens.
explanation.walkthrough: Pens look like writing tools but are enclosures; Orcadian (from Orkney, the Scottish islands) flags a Scots word, and 'Perhaps' says it is one example of a Scottish speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruives are Scottish pigsties or fish traps, enclosures for animals in the Scots dialect spoken in Orkney.

clue.text: Wide-open firm will lose its way

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so letters are removed

blocks.note: stringent means strict, firm
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A company that is completely exposed is doomed to lose its direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company but is the adjective, strict; take the street off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringent is a botanical and zoological term for gaping, as of a flower or mouth gaping widely apart.

clue.text: Wants, as some might say, large savoury snacks, mainly wraps

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular answer

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so the final letter is dropped
to wrap is to enclose, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: tapas are small Spanish savoury dishes
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone craves big savoury snacks, mostly wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: Wants looks like a verb of desire; in dialect a want is a mole, and 'as some might say' marks that regional usage. Wraps sound like food but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Talpa is the Latin and Chambers word for a mole, which dialect speakers call a want, so the animal names match.

clue.text: Bob finally asks — did Chuck cheat down under?

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: to bob is to dip the head down quickly, to duck
the closing letter of the word
hove is a past tense of heave, to throw or chuck

explanation.surface: Bob asks whether Chuck cheated while he was in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob and Chuck look like men's names; both are verbs. Down under is the familiar nickname for Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang to duck-shove means to evade responsibility or use unfair tactics, a form of cheating.

clue.text: Male frenzy ought to lead to hanky-panky

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: must expresses obligation, as ought to does
the opening letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A man in a frenzy of desire is bound to end up in some hanky-panky.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanky-panky is British slang for sexual mischief, which is apt for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Musth is the periodic state of aggressive sexual excitement in bull elephants, a frenzy affecting only males.

clue.text: Eg banana-like superb fruit essentially divided among some performers

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the middle letter is kept
items divided among a group are placed between its members

blocks.note: musos is slang for musicians
ace means excellent, superb
the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Superb bananas are shared out among a band of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divided among' means the two inserts go into different gaps of the performers word rather than together.
explanation.definitionFit: Musaceous describes plants of the banana family Musaceae, so banana-like is one example of the category.

clue.text: Power to buy and sell houses regularly buried, at one time getting through fraud

definitions.text: at one time getting through fraud

indicators.note: to house something is to give it shelter inside
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: an option is a right to buy or sell at a set price
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A dodgy property deal with buried secrets gets through by fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power to buy and sell houses' reads as an estate agent's licence, but houses is the container signal. 'At one time' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Obreption was a legal term for obtaining a dispensation or gift by false statement, i.e. acquiring something by deceit.

clue.text: Law formerly put pressure on author again?

blocks.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to rescript is to write again, a whimsical reading of author as a verb

explanation.surface: An old law once forced an author to rewrite their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' places the P on top of the down entry. The question mark admits that RESCRIPT is being read loosely as re-script; formerly marks the archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescript is an ordinance or rule laid down by authority, an older term for a decree or statute.

clue.text: Depression blocking judgment when out of work? Space needed before new start

indicators.note: out of means without, so letters are taken away
something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: an opinion is a judgment
OP is short for opus, a musical work
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Depression clouds a jobless person's judgment, who needs space before a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about unemployment; 'out of work' really removes a musical work, and the 'new start' is a new paragraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Indention is an older form of indentation, the blank gap left at the opening of a fresh paragraph.

clue.text: Hard-to-break, wily, twisting, parasitic threadworms

indicators.note: twisting round turns something back to front

blocks.note: strong means robust, hard to break
sly means cunning, wily

explanation.surface: A description of tough, cunning, wriggling worms that live off a host.
explanation.walkthrough: Every adjective seems to describe the worms, but the first two are wordplay and twisting is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongyls are nematode roundworms that live as parasites in the gut of horses and other animals.

clue.text: Provide income for now, somehow borrow tomorrow, as all do?

blocks.note: what each of the listed words does: it finishes
the two letters on which each of these four words closes

explanation.surface: Advice on finances: get money for the present by borrowing against the future, as everyone does.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words before 'as all do' each finish with the same two letters, and 'as all do' tells you what they do with them. The question mark flags this playful self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone or something is to give it a permanent fund or source of revenue.

clue.text: Former Spanish hothead, mostly amusing, maybe chops tropical tree

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
a thing that chops another splits it, going into the gap

blocks.note: fun can describe something amusing
EG, for example, signals that something is perhaps one case
the cacao tree yields cocoa beans

explanation.surface: A comical Spanish firebrand of old takes an axe to a tropical tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Maybe looks like a hedge but stands for 'for example'; the tree is split just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacafuego is an obsolete word, from Spanish, for a braggart or blusterer, literally a fire-spitter: a hot-tempered swaggerer.

clue.text: Clam following salmon is good

blocks.note: the coho is a Pacific salmon
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A seafood verdict: a clam course served after the salmon is good.
explanation.walkthrough: The clam is the definition, deriving from the wordplay that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohog is a variant spelling of quahog, the hard-shelled edible clam of the North American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Large-format book list’s half covered by money raised

indicators.note: half a word means only the front two of its four letters survive
in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top
something covered by another is enclosed within it

blocks.note: a list is an inventory
oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A large book listing half the subscribers is financed by money that has been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised money sounds like fundraising, but it means OOF turned upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a big book made from sheets folded only once, the largest common book size.

clue.text: Assess dated understanding on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so what counts is how they sound

blocks.note: sense is understanding or good judgment

explanation.surface: A critic judges an outdated grasp of things heard on a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Dated belongs with the definition, marking an obsolete sense, not with understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Cense once meant to assess or rate for taxation, related to census, a sense now archaic.

clue.text: Early US computer Wouk’s ship sent over

indicators.note: something sent over is flipped, so in a down entry it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: Herman Wouk wrote The Caine Mutiny, set aboard the USS Caine

explanation.surface: An early American computer is shipped overseas by the novelist Herman Wouk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caine Mutiny is Herman Wouk's novel about a US Navy minesweeper; in this down entry the ship's name reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: ENIAC, built in 1945, was one of the first general-purpose electronic digital machines, made in America.

clue.text: Tragic hero‘s love introduced by different (clipped) lines

indicators.note: something clipped is trimmed, so the last letter is cut off
being introduced by others means they come first

blocks.note: other means different
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A tragic hero's love affair is told in strangely cut lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines suggests verse, apt for Shakespeare, but gives two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy, the Moorish general destroyed by jealousy.

clue.text: Tramp almost pinching ribbon round centrepiece of ancient Maori ornament

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
turning something round makes it read backwards
to pinch is to grip tight, so one piece holds another
the centrepiece is what lies in the middle, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: to tramp is to walk a long way, to hike
a tie is a ribbon or band
the central letter of the word's seven

explanation.surface: A tramp nearly steals a ribbon wound round an old Maori trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: HIK, the walk cut short, holds EIT, and the I from the middle of ancient closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hei-tiki is a carved greenstone pendant shaped like a human figure, worn round the neck by Maori people.

clue.text: Sign at either end of passage in westbound congestion

definitions.text: Sign at either end of passage

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words
westbound in an across clue means travelling right to left

blocks.note: the letters run backwards across the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A road sign warns of a jam at both ends of a passage heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is long and reads like a traffic notice; the answer is buried backwards in a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a segno is a mark showing where a repeated section begins or ends, bounding a passage.

clue.text: Brought back discipline, increasing strength of an army

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the other way, so it reads right to left

blocks.note: arts are branches of learning, disciplines
a tonic is something that invigorates or builds strength

explanation.surface: Restoring discipline makes a fighting force stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface sounds military, but discipline means a field of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratonic is a rare adjective, from Greek stratos, describing things belonging to a military host.
